status: USER-REPORTED fixed-tic hardware results; one run per variant
transcription: Revision, measured count, D00E, mean frame/decode/present times, final tic and frame hash manually read from original photographs and enlarged crops. Min/max timings are deliberately not transcribed in this mean-only result.
user_observation: V46 was clearly faster; the user corrected C46 to V46.
interpretation: Both variants completed 30 measured frames at tic 40 with the expected EBC8D404 frame sequence. The comparison retains the same reduced-detail assets.
Mean frame time fell 1147 to 205 ms, an 82.13% time reduction and about 5.60 times the reciprocal mean rate. Mean DEFLATE time fell 864 to zero; presentation stayed 99 ms.

V46 is about 3.05 times the reciprocal mean rate of the previous V44 result (626 ms). This cross-version comparison includes reduced asset detail as well as storage changes and is not an isolated codec comparison.
V45 is slower than V44. Their assets, pack/page layout and forced-raw page selection differ; the data does not show that reducing detail alone improves the compressed path.

The remaining 205 ms consists of 99 ms measured presentation and about 106 ms outside it. The latter includes simulation, rendering, raw asset reads, copies and other work; it is not a pure renderer measurement.

The reciprocal rate of about 4.88 frames/s describes this fixed-tic start-room benchmark, not measured normal-play FPS. Controls, movement, other scenes and long-term stability require hardware tests.
No CPU/PLL/SFC or LCD divider change was requested between these two builds; their actual frequencies remain unmeasured.

The current indexed present loop waits for final DMA completion before returning, so rendering the next frame does not overlap the prior frame presentation. Using released SRAM for a second indexed surface and cooperative DMA service is a candidate, not implemented or measured here.
